scope: Curated neuronal-current MRI, MRCDI, MREIT and related simulation literature; not a systematic review.

sources.title: Existence and Uniqueness for Electrode Models for Electric Current Computed Tomography
sources.authors: Somersalo, Erkki and Cheney, Margaret and Isaacson, David
sources.finding: Classical complete electrode model and its existence/uniqueness foundation for current-driven conductivity problems.
sources.limitation: Mathematical foundation, not MRI acquisition or validation of this repository's discretization.
sources.verification: SIAM publisher metadata/abstract inspected 26 October 2026; full proof not independently reproduced.

sources.title: Applications of the duality theory of convex analysis to the complete electrode model of electrical impedance tomography
sources.authors: Díaz-Avalos, Josué D.
sources.evidence: duality and a posteriori numerical analysis
sources.finding: Develops a current-field dual formulation and CEM error estimates, with finite-element numerical examples.
sources.limitation: No MRI validation. The tensor reconstruction and numerical energy bracket here are separately implemented and tested, not a reproduction of this paper's experiments.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract and metadata inspected 26 October 2026; full numerical implementation not reproduced.

sources.title: Neuronal current distribution imaging using magnetic resonance
sources.authors: Kamei, H. and Iramina, K. and Yoshikawa, K. and Ueno, S.
sources.evidence: early human claim and phantom work
sources.finding: Precedes the San Antonio msMRI report and is essential for a careful priority discussion.
sources.limitation: Does not establish a generally reproducible human method.
sources.verification: Metadata and historical role cross-checked in Xiong 2003 and original coauthor Ueno's 2021 account, DOI 10.1029/2020RS007152; original full text not inspected.

sources.title: Toward direct mapping of neuronal activity: MRI detection of ultraweak, transient magnetic field changes
sources.authors: Bodurka, Jerzy and Bandettini, Peter A.
sources.finding: Transient-field phase encoding using spin-echo timing.
sources.limitation: Known imposed waveform and geometry; no human neuronal validation.
sources.verification: Publisher-hosted paper text and NIMH author presentation.

sources.title: Directly mapping magnetic field effects of neuronal activity by magnetic resonance imaging
sources.authors: Xiong, Jinhu and Fox, Peter T. and Gao, Jia-Hong
sources.finding: San Antonio visuomotor msMRI paper matching the user's recollection.
sources.limitation: Historical claim; later negative evidence must accompany it.
sources.verification: PMC text and author-hosted PDF, including affiliations.

sources.title: Hunting for neuronal currents: absence of rapid MRI signal changes during visual-evoked response
sources.authors: Chu, Renxin and de Zwart, Jacco A. and van Gelderen, Peter and Fukunaga, Masaki and Kellman, Peter and Holroyd, Tom and Duyn, Jeff H.
sources.finding: Explicitly tests rapid current effects versus slower BOLD effects.
sources.limitation: A negative result bounds its acquisition and task, not every possible future sequence.
sources.verification: Author-hosted paper text.

sources.title: Magnetic resonance electrical impedance tomography at 3 Tesla field strength
sources.authors: Oh, Suk H. and others
sources.finding: Early clinical-field-strength MREIT milestone.
sources.limitation: Conductivity measurement with injected current is a different problem from passive neural recording.
sources.verification: PubMed metadata and abstract.

sources.title: Direct detection of neuronal activity with MRI: Fantasy, possibility, or reality?
sources.authors: Bandettini, Peter A. and Petridou, Natalia and Bodurka, Jerzy
sources.finding: The key Bandettini-group synthesis of the early debate.
sources.limitation: Predates later replication studies and method developments.
sources.verification: Official NIMH record; DOI cross-checked in later primary-paper references.

sources.title: Direct magnetic resonance detection of neuronal electrical activity
sources.authors: Petridou, Natalia and Plenz, Dietmar and Silva, Afonso C. and Loew, Murray and Bodurka, Jerzy and Bandettini, Peter A.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.finding: Blood-free rat cultures, electrophysiology and blockade controls support activity-linked MR signals.
sources.limitation: Controlled cultures do not establish intact-human feasibility.
sources.verification: PubMed and indexed PMC methods/discussion.

sources.title: Finding neuroelectric activity under magnetic-field oscillations (NAMO) with magnetic resonance imaging in vivo
sources.authors: Truong, Trong-Kha and Song, Allen W.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.finding: Oscillating-gradient encoding with a Lorentz-effect interpretation.
sources.limitation: Requires electromechanical modeling; not established cerebral current imaging.
sources.verification: Indexed PMC methods and discussion.

sources.title: Realistic simulations of neuronal activity: a contribution to the debate on direct detection of neuronal currents by MRI
sources.authors: Cassarà, A. M. and Hagberg, G. E. and Bianciardi, M. and Migliore, M. and Maraviglia, B.
sources.finding: Realistic morphology and population assumptions change predicted MR effects.
sources.limitation: A model-based forecast depends on the chosen neuronal ensemble and activity. Online 2007; issue 2008.
sources.verification: PubMed metadata/abstract and authors' 2007 ISMRM precursor.

sources.title: Neuronal current imaging: sensitivity of magnitude and spatial distribution to changes in current timing
sources.authors: Drobnjak, I. and Pell, G. and Jenkinson, M.
sources.finding: Direct historical link between POSSUM and neuronal-current timing studies.
sources.limitation: Conference abstract; use the 2010 full paper for the developed method.
sources.verification: Official proceedings PDF.

sources.title: Magnetic resonance electrical impedance tomography (MREIT) for high-resolution conductivity imaging
sources.authors: Woo, Eung Je and Seo, Jin Keun
sources.finding: Useful account of the foundational theory and experimental program.
sources.limitation: Historical source; not a measure of present clinical adoption.
sources.verification: PubMed and accessible paper text.

sources.title: In vivo high-resolution conductivity imaging of the human leg using MREIT: the first human experiment
sources.authors: Kim, Hyung Joong and others
sources.finding: Human conductivity-imaging milestone during the remembered development period.
sources.limitation: Leg protocol and scaled conductivity reconstruction do not transfer directly to the brain.
sources.verification: PubMed metadata and abstract.

sources.title: Simulating the effects of time-varying magnetic fields with a realistic simulated scanner
sources.authors: Drobnjak, Ivana and Pell, Gaby S. and Jenkinson, Mark
sources.finding: Time-varying-field extension of POSSUM; timing can alter image appearance away from a conductor.
sources.limitation: Wire validation establishes encoding behavior, not realistic neural-source strength.
sources.verification: Oxford Research Archive publication record and abstract; official FSL documentation.

sources.title: Magnetic Resonance Electrical Impedance Tomography (MREIT)
sources.authors: Seo, Jin Keun and Woo, Eung Je
sources.finding: Explains the move toward internal magnetic data and Bz-based reconstruction.
sources.limitation: Mathematical guarantees are conditional on the measurement/model assumptions.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract and metadata.

sources.title: Direct neural current imaging in an intact cerebellum with magnetic resonance imaging

sources.finding: Phase response and source estimates compared with concurrent LFP measurements.

sources.verification: PubMed metadata and indexed PMC methods/results.

sources.title: Direct detection of neural activity in vitro using magnetic resonance electrical impedance tomography (MREIT)
sources.authors: Sadleir, Rosalind J. and Fu, Fanrui and Falgas, Corey and Holland, Stephen and Boggess, May and Grant, Samuel C. and Woo, Eung Je
sources.finding: Activity-related phase variability depends on the imaging-current condition.
sources.limitation: Conductivity-probing mechanism, not passive human current imaging.
sources.verification: PubMed abstract and indexed PMC methods/conclusions.

sources.title: Human in-vivo brain magnetic resonance current density imaging (MRCDI)

sources.finding: Human brain current-field measurement relevant to electrical stimulation.

sources.title: Low-Frequency Conductivity Tensor Imaging of the Human Head in vivo using DT-MREIT: First Study
sources.authors: Chauhan, Munish and others
sources.finding: Combines electrical magnetic-field measurements with diffusion tensor information.
sources.limitation: Tensor reconstruction is constrained by the assumed relation between diffusion and conductivity.
sources.verification: PMC metadata and indexed methods.

sources.title: Functional magnetic resonance electrical impedance tomography (fMREIT) sensitivity analysis using an active bidomain finite-element model of neural tissue
sources.authors: Sadleir, Rosalind J. and Fu, Fanrui and Chauhan, Munish

sources.verification: PubMed abstract and publisher metadata.

sources.title: Toward direct MRI of neuro-electro-magnetic oscillations in the human brain

sources.title: Detection of nanotesla AC magnetic fields using steady-state SIRS and ultra-low field MRI

sources.title: Computational and Phantom-Based Feasibility Study of 3D dcNCI With Ultra-Low-Field MRI

sources.authors: Göksu, Cihan and others

sources.title: In vivo direct imaging of neuronal activity at high temporospatial resolution
sources.authors: Toi, Phan Tan and others
sources.finding: Historically influential DIANA report.
sources.limitation: RETRACTED 2025-09-25; see 10.1126/science.aec1773. Do not use as validated positive evidence.
sources.verification: PubMed retracted-publication record and linked retraction notice.

sources.title: Initial experiences with Direct Imaging of Neuronal Activity (DIANA) in humans
sources.authors: Hodono, S. and Rideaux, R. and van Kerkoerle, T. and Cloos, M. A.
sources.finding: Examines translation and acquisition behavior in humans.
sources.limitation: Does not establish a reliable human DIANA modality.
sources.verification: Indexed PMC article and author preprint; DOI in primary-paper references.

sources.title: High-resolution Dynamic Human Brain Neural Activity Recording Using 3T MRI
sources.authors: Zhang, Yifei and others
sources.finding: Proposes rapid stimulus-synchronized human acquisition.
sources.limitation: No peer-reviewed successor or independent confirmation identified in this search.
sources.verification: bioRxiv full text and author institutional announcement.

sources.title: Can MRI Be Used as a Sensor to Record Neural Activity?
sources.authors: Roth, Bradley J.

sources.limitation: Predates DIANA retraction and the 2026 evidence; some outlook statements are speculative.
sources.verification: PubMed and accessible review text.

sources.title: Volumetric measurements of weak current-induced magnetic fields in the human brain at high resolution

sources.limitation: Mechanism-specific artifact demonstration, not a universal MRI impossibility result.
sources.verification: PubMed metadata and abstract; official ISMRM abstract.

sources.title: Retraction
sources.authors: Toi, Phan Tan and Jang, Hyun Jae and Min, Kyeongseon and Kim, Sung-Phil and Lee, Seung-Kyun and Lee, Jongho and Kwag, Jeehyun and Park, Jang-Yeon

sources.limitation: Keep original and notice linked in bibliographies.

sources.verification: arXiv v2 dated 2026-09-22 and PubMed record.
